atoms.word: V i k i n g

feedback.finish: Viking is an Old Norse word meaning “a pirate raid”. During the Viking age of AD 700 to 1100, many of these fearsome warriors came to our shores.

atoms.b: Vikings were people who came from Scandinavia, an area in Northern Europe that includes the countries Denmark, ((++Norway Australia)) and Sweden.

The Vikings left their homes in Scandinavia and travelled by ((++boat aeroplane)) to Britain. They carried out lots of violent raids in Britain, before eventually settling in an area called the Danelaw.

hint.label: Raid
hint.text: A raid is a surprise attack that usually involves stealing.

atoms.b: The most important city in the Danelaw was Jorvik, which we now know as ((++York Wales)). Over 10,000 people lived there, and it was an important place for trading goods.

instruction.text: The Vikings and Anglo-Saxons both originally came from similar areas of Northern Europe. What do you think this means?

feedback.end: Anglo-Saxons and Vikings had similar languages and once shared similar Pagan religions. However, by the time the Vikings arrived in Britain, most Anglo-Saxons had converted to Christianity.

b.sound: They shared lots of similarities with each other.

instruction.text: Apart from being warriors, what other jobs do you think Vikings had?

feedback.end: Most people only think of Vikings as strong warriors, but they also worked ordinary jobs in farming and crafts.

instruction.text: Find the writing on the stone.

atoms.b: This stone has runes carved into it. Runes were the ((++written spoken)) language of the Vikings and have been found carved into stones, jewellery, weapons and more.
Vikings used runes to label their belongings or the goods that they traded. They also wrote the names of ((++dead living)) people on gravestones.

trainers.instruction: This is the runic alphabet that the Vikings used. Use the alphabet to decode the answers to the questions.
